_why: [R-ENF-02] ratchet for scripts/check_site_data_reader.py. Files reading assets/data.js by regular expression when the shared reader was adopted (03-Sep-2026). The rule [R-ENF-03] predates this list by four weeks and bound in the two places somebody had implemented it. MAY ONLY EVER SHORTEN (--prune).
_repointed: 03-Sep-2026: the gate's population keyed on the STRING "data.js" and so listed three files that never open it — two carrying the word inside an external-reader scrub list and one in a prose comment. Re-pointed at a PATH CONSTRUCTION per [R-COC-01] and the three removed; the population fell 44 -> 31 because the word appears in prose far more often than the file is read.
_repointed_twice: 03-Sep-2026: a WRITER cannot read data.js through a parse and still write it — string surgery is the only sound way to preserve the file's formatting and its prose comments — so holding the three writers to the reader's rule made them a debt that could never be paid, which is the permanently-red check [R-ENF-02] forbids. The clause was re-pointed at what a writer actually owes: proof that the PARSER agrees with what it wrote. That surfaced FOUR MORE writers the string predicate never counted, one of them (refresh_cone_one.py, a cone writer) with no post-write check of any kind, not even node --check.
